source.title: Interactions between frontal cortex and basal ganglia in working memory: a computational model.

confidence_rationale: Directly grounds ARC-063's availability-vs-expression DISTINCTION: the basal ganglia provide a selective, dynamic GATE on which frontal representations are UPDATED/maintained (become available), separate from selecting the final action. Higher mapping_fidelity than the threshold papers because gating-of-availability is exactly the function, not just an analog.
failure_signatures: The gated content is task-relevant working-memory representations, not labelled rules; REE assumes the same gate type can admit a CandidateRule, which the model does not test.

Gating is binary/selective per stripe in the model; ARC-063's tolerance gate is graded/threshold-based -- the model grounds the gating FUNCTION but not the graded-tolerance form (the threshold papers cover the graded part).

mapping.source_claim_statement: The basal ganglia contribute a selective, dynamic gating function that enables frontal (PFC) memory representations to be rapidly updated in a task-relevant manner, while PFC provides robust active maintenance -- a 'releasing the brakes' disinhibition that decides WHEN a representation enters/updates the active maintained set.
mapping.ree_translation: This grounds the KEY distinction in ARC-063 element (ii): tolerance-gated AVAILABILITY (which candidate rule becomes active/maintained, gated by the basal ganglia) is architecturally separate from rule EXPRESSION/selection (which action is taken). ARC-063's CandidateRule field availability gate maps onto BG-gated updating of PFC rule_state -- exactly the SD-033a rule_state-into-PFC pathway GAP-B needs populated.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The model gates working-memory CONTENT updating, not the admission of a labelled rule; and its gate is selective/binary rather than graded-by-tolerance. It grounds the gating FUNCTION and the availability-vs-selection split, while the conflict-scaled graded threshold comes from the Cavanagh/Frank STN papers.
mapping.source_context: Computational neural-network model of frontal-cortex / basal-ganglia interaction on a selective working-memory-updating (continuous performance) task.

confidence_components.notes: Canonical PBWM-lineage model. Mapping fidelity higher than the threshold papers: gating-of-availability is the literal function. Transfer risk lower (general WM mechanism, not clinical).
